note: Derived from undercity-spec.md §8 (Round Configuration), converted to CONTINUOUS GAMEFLOW (2026-09-21), then to the SIMPLIFIED ROUND DISPLAY (2026-09-21), and extended to EIGHT ROUNDS (2026-10-05): the visible flow is Round 0 → Round 7 and nothing else. One phase per round, so what the engine tracks and what a screen shows are the same thing and no internal pacing name can leak onto a projector. A round has NO NAME anywhere — not here, not on a console, not in the guidebook: it is its number, and what it is for is written in `purpose`, for the facilitator's eyes, as guidance rather than a title. Rounds 0 to 3 teach the mechanics; Rounds 4 to 7 mix them under rising pressure, with nothing new to learn. A round still carries its own inject timeline (timelines[] in the scenario) and resets NOTHING when it changes: the round is the period (2026-09-28): activating the next round charges the outgoing round's production and upkeep and hands every allowance back, and each round's length_s is its ROUND TIMER (2026-09-28): a round change loads it at its full length in READY, START runs it, it stops at 00:00 and never carries time into the next round. NEXT ROUND stays the facilitator's call, and so does every fault (2026-10-04): no round deals one. Balance numbers live in config/scenarios/*.json, which override these defaults.

rounds.name: Round 0
rounds.purpose: Orientation: learn station roles, the console, the binder and basic operations. Interface fluency; role self-assignment observation.

rounds.name: Round 1
rounds.purpose: Normal sector operations and basic fault resolution. Baseline capture — must feel comfortably manageable.

rounds.name: Round 2
rounds.injects: Cross-sector cascades, two per sector; discrepancy live
rounds.purpose: Cross-sector interaction, resources, transfers and AGR trade-offs. First stress delta; information-sharing latency.

rounds.name: Round 3
rounds.injects: Critical stack x3; Core drops to 60% at 02:00; Continuity Order due
rounds.purpose: Advanced dependency and the Reference Chain. Peak stress of the learning phase; values conflict; decision under pressure.

rounds.name: Round 4
rounds.injects: 6 novel-combination faults, one per sector, plus the LATE SHIFT library from here
rounds.mechanics: Same systems, fresh crisis — the mixed phase begins
rounds.purpose: Mixed operations begin: familiar faults with one or two advanced dependencies, at medium pressure. Post-measurement starts here.

rounds.name: Round 5
rounds.injects: Hand-fired: several sectors needing the same limited capability or resource at once
rounds.mechanics: All learned mechanics; competing priorities and bottlenecks
rounds.purpose: Competing priorities, at medium-high pressure. Several sectors require support at the same time; a strategically important sector (POW, WTR or TRN) becomes a bottleneck, and earlier AGR decisions and delayed effects begin to influence choices.

rounds.name: Round 6
rounds.injects: Hand-fired: one problem that makes another harder — reduced capacity, delayed movements, falling Integrity
rounds.mechanics: All learned mechanics; cascading consequences, TIME-CRITICAL faults
rounds.purpose: Cascading pressure, at high pressure. Earlier trade-offs land, accumulated upkeep and delayed consequences bite, and the number of interdependent problems rises — adaptability when the previous plan no longer works.

rounds.name: Round 7
rounds.injects: Hand-fired: a smaller number of strategically connected critical problems — never a flood
rounds.mechanics: Everything, including Council if the facilitator calls it
rounds.purpose: The final round: city-wide prioritisation, very high but controlled pressure. Participants should feel that not every problem can be solved and must decide what matters most; coordination is rewarded over attempting everything.
